issues.source_quote: Тики так! Как стемнеет, будем брать!
issues.translation_quote: Tick-tock! Once it's dark, we take it!
issues.justification: "Тики-так" is thieves' slang for "okay / all right", taught in the vocabulary lesson as the equivalent of "Хорошо?". "Tick-tock" evokes a clock and gives English viewers no clue it means "OK". The slang-lesson gag ("Good? - Tick-tock") and the later "All right! I mean, tick-tock" lose their sense.

issues.source_quote: Все! Кина не будет. Электричество кончилось.
issues.translation_quote: That's it! No movie tonight. Power's out.
issues.justification: This is a famous quote, and the Russian film-slang spelling "кина" gives it a colloquial, jokey flavor. The English is flat and neutral.
The meaning is "nothing to congratulate me on". "Don't." is curt and unclear, and it doesn't convey that the arrests led nowhere.
The source speaker uses normal, if rough, Russian. Pidgin grammar here is inconsistent with the rest of the dialogue and misleadingly suggests the broken-speech voice of Vasya.

issues.source_quote: Это фамилия, а имя - Василий Алибабаевич, Вася.
issues.translation_quote: That's surname, and name is Vasily Alibabayevich, Vasya.
issues.justification: The speaker (the educated Troshkin) has fluent, correct Russian. Dropping the articles makes his English broken and out of character.

issues.source_quote: А Гаврила Петрович по фене ругается!
issues.translation_quote: Gavrila Petrovich is swearing in slang!
issues.justification: "По фене ругается" means he is using thieves' cant or criminal jargon, which has just been banned. "Swearing in slang" is vaguer and changes the sense.
The rhyming wordplay (летчик/налетчик, "pilot/raider") is lost. "Pilferer" is also too mild and bookish for the speaker.

This is a culturally specific film and song allusion meaning "standing out in plain view", and it is transferred literally. It will confuse a general English audience without a gloss or an adapted idiom.
A mistranslated or opaque fragment; the shouted cry in a fight has no clear sense in English.
The Soviet economic-crimes police unit is left as an unexplained acronym. English viewers cannot recognize the gag that the speaker is naming the police.

issues.source_quote: Это что-то вроде конкурса на звание лучшего Бармалея.
issues.translation_quote: It's something like a contest for the best Barmaley.
issues.justification: The Chukovsky villain reference is transliterated with no cultural cue. English audiences will not get the joke about a scary costume.
